Right: the four-cycle A, B, C, D (in the accent color) cannot be split that way, so is_split_graph() returns False." width="100%"} A graph is *split* when its nodes can be divided into a clique (every pair joined) and an independent set (no pair joined), with any edges at all between the two parts. Stars, complete graphs and threshold graphs are split; the square and the five-cycle are not. Split graphs are exactly the graphs that are chordal with a chordal complement, and they model core-periphery structure in its purest form: a fully connected core and a periphery whose members link only to the core. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is split. The empty graph is. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~is_complete_split_graph`) : Split, with every clique node joined to every other node. [](`~is_chordal`) : Split graphs are the chordal graphs with a chordal complement. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Hammer and Simeone (1981) showed that being split depends only on the degree sequence. With the degrees sorted in decreasing order $d_1 \ge \dots \ge d_n$ and $m$ the largest $i$ with $d_i \ge i - 1$, the graph is split exactly when $\sum_{i \le m} d_i = m(m - 1) + \sum_{i > m} d_i$, in which case the $m$ nodes of highest degree form the clique. This takes $O(V \log V + E)$ time. Results match NetworkX pull request #8126's `is_split_graph`, which tests that the graph and its complement are both chordal. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A triangle with a pendant node is split, with the triangle as the clique and the pendant node as the independent set, while the square is not: ::: {#86b1c7df .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec kite = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) kite.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) kite.is_split_graph(), ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(4).is_split_graph() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
